en.content:
The recent joint operation by the Independent Commission Against Corruption and the police, which led to 42 arrests over alleged triad infiltration of building maintenance projects, is a stark reminder that public safety depends as much on the integrity of systems as on physical infrastructure. The arrests come against the backdrop of the Tai Po tragedy and mounting public anger over disabled alarms and suspected malfeasance. Decisive law enforcement action is necessary not only to hold individuals to account but also to reassure a grieving community that the rule of law will be applied without fear or favour.

Yet arrests alone will not be sufficient. The episode has exposed weaknesses in procurement, oversight and estate governance that have allowed corrupt practices to take root. Contracting processes for large-scale repairs and maintenance need clearer safeguards: transparent tenders, rigorous vetting of contractors, routine independent audits and mandatory reporting of conflicts of interest. Licensing and performance monitoring of fire-safety firms should be reviewed and strengthened so that lapses in duty cannot be dismissed as routine failings. All reforms must respect due process while prioritising the safety of residents.

Equally important is the role of government and community institutions in restoring trust. The administration’s moves to appoint an estate manager, hold briefings for affected residents and encourage the public to share information with the inquiry are steps in the right direction. Victims and their families deserve timely compensation, practical assistance and clear explanations of remedial measures. Citizens should be encouraged — through protected, accessible channels — to report suspected corrupt practices, knowing that their contributions are taken seriously and handled professionally.

This moment calls for a balanced combination of enforcement, institutional reform and social solidarity. Hong Kong’s strengths have long lain in competent public institutions and a civic culture that values rule-bound governance; these must be mobilised now to close loopholes, deter organised crime’s economic footholds and make safety non-negotiable. If the community, watchdogs and government can convert outrage into sustained, practical improvements, the city will be better protected and more resilient for it.
en.topic_title: Hong Kong anti-graft watchdog, police arrest 42 in crackdown on triad-linked building maintenance syndicate

zh.content:
香港社會喺太和、灣福大火之後，對建築維修工程入面嘅黑渠、三合會滲透，一直好憂慮。今次廉署同警方聯手拘捕42人，係當局用法治手段回應公眾關切嘅明顯行動，亦顯示政府唔會容忍以黑市化手法侵蝕公共安全與市民利益。面對168位死者嘅慘劇，社會需要見到果斷執法，以重建公眾對制度嘅信心，追究責任、清理亂象，係合理同必要嘅步驟。

但單憑拘捕並不足夠，問題係結構性。工程招標、監管、付款同驗收嘅流程若然仍然存在灰色地帶，或者欠缺透明度，黑色勢力與中介就有可乘之機。政府與業界應該加快檢視制度漏洞：由招標資訊公開化、電子化監控、強化資格審查到更落實的審計與追責機制，都係要做嘅功課。同時，保護吹哨人、鼓勵居民同工人舉報問題，能夠補上官方調查以外嘅社會監察力量。

處理此事亦要兼顧受害者與社區復元。要確保受災居民獲得足夠嘅賠償、安置同心理支援，並且令屋苑管理結構更透明、公正，避免同類風險重演。業界亦應提升從業人員嘅專業操守與合規文化，政府可以考慮加強培訓、設立行業守則同罰則，讓「安全第一」真正落地。

總括而言，拘捕行動係正確而且必要，亦符合依法治港嘅原則；但更長遠嘅挑戰係制度與文化重建。政府、執法部門、業界同市民要同步出力，既要嚴打黑惡勢力入侵公共工程嘅空間，亦要把預防機制建立得更實在，務求由根本上保障市民生命財產安全。

en.topic_title: 13 parents, middleman jailed for up to 14 months over bribes to secure priority admission to international kindergarten
en.topic_summary:
Thirteen parents and a middleman have been jailed for up to one year and two months for offering HK$1.1 million in bribes to secure admission to an English Schools Foundation (ESF) kindergarten.



West Kowloon Law Courts Building. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP.



The defendants, aged between 36 and 48, were sentenced at the West Kowloon Law Courts Building on Tuesday. They were found guilty in February of bribing an administrator at ESF Wu Kai Sha International Kindergarten in Ma On Shan.
